response: Yes, a family meetings intervention can help prevent depression and anxiety in family caregivers of dementia patients. This type of intervention typically involves regular meetings with a healthcare professional, such as a social worker or nurse, to provide emotional support, education, and guidance on caregiving strategies. Studies have shown that family meetings interventions can reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety in family caregivers, improve their overall well-being, and enhance their ability to care for their loved ones with dementia.
